candidates.name: Tibidabo Mountain amusement park
candidates.content: Tibidabo is a popular attraction with stunning vistas, an historic amusement park, and the iconic Sagrat Cor church.

candidates.name: Mercat del Born
candidates.content: This market was the central market for Barcelona until 1973 and its closing marked the beginning of the neighborhood's decline before its current resurgence. While undergoing renovations, whole streets and homes that had been demo

candidates.name: Picasso Museum
candidates.price: Adults €13 (on-line €12) , discount for students having student ID & 65+, free on the first Sunday each month, free every Thursday evening from 18:00 to 21:30. Advance booking recommended (including free-of-charge times)
candidates.hours: Sun-Tue 10:00-20:00 (19:00 in winter), closes strictly on time, visitors are asked to exit 10 minutes before closing time. free at certain times, see website.
candidates.content: Has a lot of art from his first period, before the cubism, but almost none of his most famous works. Pictures are described only in Spanish, but overview texts for each period are available in English. Luggage over 30x30cm needs t

candidates.name: Palau Güell
candidates.price: €12 (audio guide included); tickets booth at 1 Nou de la Rambla closes 1 hr earlier; also online
candidates.content: Palace designed by Gaudí for the industrial tycoon Eusebi Güell. There is a basement and three levels of the palace to explore, the highest featuring a small exhibition. It is in a different style to Gaudí's apartment blocks La Pe

candidates.name: Maritime Museum
candidates.price: 10€ - 18€. Free every Sunday after 3:00 pm. The exhibits in the entrance hall and the Espai Mirador are free of charge
candidates.content: Housed in Drassanes, the Gothic shipyard of the city. During the 14th century, the Aragó Crown was the most important power in the Mediterranean Sea, and this was the main place where the ships were built. Nowadays, it's th

candidates.name: Sant Pau del Camp
candidates.content: A rare example of Romanesque architecture, the prettiest in Barcelona. Its name reflects the fact that the church was once surrounded by green fields outside the city walls.

candidates.name: Museu de les Il·lusions
candidates.content: A museum of more than 30 room-sized, hand-painted 3D murals built on forced perspective: visitors stand on marked spots and appear to hang from a dragon's jaw or teeter over a painted canyon. Photography is the point of the visit.

candidates.name: Aquàrium de Barcelona
candidates.content: The second biggest aquarium in Europe. Watch thousands of fish, penguins and sharks in this interactive sea-life museum. Unlike Genoese Aquarium it has a long glass tube, where you can walk watching sharks and other fish swimming

candidates.name: Parc Zoològic de Barcelona
candidates.content: This zoo was famous for its albino gorilla Snowflake prior to his death. Today this zoo still has many other features including a science museum inside the zoo.

candidates.name: Sagrada Família
candidates.alt: Basílica i Temple Expiatori de la Sagrada Família
candidates.price: €26 for adult, with audio guide, €30 if tour included. €10 extra to visit the towers
candidates.content: Barcelona's most popular and famous attraction, the Sagrada Família is a testament to Antonio Gaudi's modernist style and unlike any other church in the world. The texture and detail on the façades are intricate and incorporate fo

candidates.name: Casa Vicens
candidates.hours: Mon 10:00-15:00, last admission 13:40, Tue-Sun 10:00-19:00, last admission 17:40
candidates.content: The first building Gaudi built in Barcelona. It has been opened as a museum. It's possible to walk the whole monumental enclosure, including the garden and the interior of the building. In UNESCO World Heritage Sites list since 20

candidates.name: Monestir de Pedralbes
candidates.price: €5; reduced €3.50. 1st Su of the month and Su after 15:00 free
candidates.content: A beautiful Gothic monastery near the university, there are a museum which depicts the monastery life, a church, and a marvelous chapel covered with medieval frescoes.

candidates.name: MMACA - Museu de Matemàtiques de Catalunya
candidates.hours: Wed 17:00-20:00; Sun 10:00-14:00. Sometimes open on additional days but closed during school holidays.
candidates.content: The museum has limited opening hours but the park it is situated in is also interesting. Check website before going to the museum as it will eventually relocate to The Can Bagaria building.

candidates.name: Futbol Club Barcelona Museum
candidates.price: €25 (€20 for people from 6-13 and >70 years old)
candidates.hours: 09:00-19:00; Dec 25, Jan 1 closed (deviating on match days)
candidates.content: Museum dedicated to the FC Barcelona. It occupies 3,500 m² and attracts 1.2 million visitors a year, ranking it second to the Museu Picasso, which attracts 1.3 million visitors, as the most visited museum in the city of Barcelona.

candidates.name: DHub Disseny Hub Barcelona
candidates.price: General admission/reduced admission: permanent exhibitions €6 reduced €4; temporary exhibitions €4.40/3; combined permanent and temporary exhibitions €8/5.50. Tickets valid for any 2 days within the 6 months following purchase.
candidates.content: Much to the dismay of Mickey Mouse aficionados, Disseny is Catalan for "design", not "Disney". The "Disseny Hub" houses the amalgamated museums focusing on applied arts and design, including Museu de les Arts Decoratives, Museu de

candidates.name: Museu de Ciències Naturals de Barcelona
candidates.hours: Oct-May: Tue-Fri 10:00-19:00; Sat Sun 10:00-20;00; June-Sept: Tue-Sun 10:00-21:00
candidates.content: Museum with a number of exhibitions about the Earth and its natural history. One exhibit covers the origin of life on Earth and how it has evolved. A second exhibit deals with nature and life on Earth today. The third exhibit cove

candidates.name: Barcelona Pavilion
candidates.price: General public €8, student €4; under 16 free; annual subscription €20; entrance fee for groups: groups of more than 15 people with reservation required €6; architectural tour with reservation required €90; discounts: 25% off with Bus Turístic, Barcelona Card and Barcelona City Tour (2022)
candidates.content: The Pavilion is one of the emblematic works of Mies van der Rohe and key reference architecture of the twentieth century. The famous German Pavilion was designed for the 1929 Barcelona International Exhibition and reconstructed in

candidates.name: National Art Museum of Catalonia
candidates.price: Adult €12, under 16 or over 65 (EU resident) free, including two visits within 30 days. First Sunday each month is free for everyone. Included in the Barcelona Art Passport
candidates.content: Has the single best collection of Romanesque art in the world, and a fine Gothic collection as well. Includes the Pantocrator from the Taüll Romanesque church. The building itself is also very beautiful.

candidates.name: Basilica of Santa Maria del Mar
candidates.content: One of the most representative examples of Catalan Gothic architecture, it features a sombre but beautiful interior. The upsweeping verticality and lightness of the interior are especially surprising considering the blocky exterio

candidates.name: Carrer Montcada
candidates.content: This street has the biggest collection of Gothic houses in Barcelona. In amongst these houses is the Picasso Museum, which is definitely worth a visit. There are also smaller museums along the street, and many tapas restaurants th

candidates.name: Passeig del Born
candidates.content: This avenue goes from the Santa Maria del Mar church to the Born market and is where the legendary jousting matches of the Middle Ages took place, as well as numerous fairs and marches. This is also where men were knighted. It is

candidates.name: Plaça Sant Jaume
candidates.content: This square has been the political hub since the Roman era. It has been witness to some of the most important events in modern Catalan history, such as the proclamation of the Catalan State in 1931. At one end, there is the Palace

candidates.name: Plaça del Rei
candidates.content: This square has two important buildings, the Santa Àgata church, where the kings from the Aragon crown had baptism. Is possible to visit it. The other building has the Saló del Tinell, one of the best civil Gothic architecture exa

candidates.name: Plaça Sant Felip Neri
candidates.content: One of the most romantic squares in Barcelona, it hides a dark history in that it was built over the city's old cemetery. Barcelona's most famous architect, Antonio Gaudi, was on his way to visit the church there when he was run o

candidates.name: Plaça del Pi
candidates.content: This square next to La Rambla is one of the prettiest parts of the quarter. It has a pine tree in the middle (Pi mines pine tree), the church of Santa Maria del Pi, which is a very pretty Gothic church with a huge rose window. Man

candidates.name: Museu d'Història de la Ciutat de Barcelona
candidates.content: Includes access to underground Roman ruins and a complex of historic buildings in the centre of the Barri Gòtic (Gothic Quarter), and is a reasonably good historical museum.

candidates.name: Museu de l'Eròtica de Barcelona
candidates.content: Museum dedicated to erotic and sensual works. A huge tourist trap. The tour is not worth it, unless you wish to see old paintings of the Kama Sutra. The only interest is the huge phallus in the hallway, which makes for funny pictu

candidates.name: Hash Marijuana & Hemp Museum Barcelona
candidates.content: This museum in the modernist Palau Mornau offers a unique permanent exhibition on the development of the cannabis plant as a versatile source for industrial, nutritional, medicinal, sacramental and recreational purposes.

candidates.name: Sónar
candidates.price: €52 daypass, €76 night entry, €199 festival pass on internet booking, higher fees for entrance passes
candidates.content: An annual three-day music festival. It is described officially as a festival of Advanced Music and Multimedia Art. Music is by far the main aspect of the festival. The festival runs for three days and nights, usually starting on a

candidates.name: Monegros Desert Festival
candidates.content: The most famous and biggest one day/night electronic music festivals in Spain is in the desert of Fraga, from Barcelona. More than 40,000 people gather every July to celebrate electronic music with the best DJs representing styles

candidates.name: Festes de la Mercè
candidates.content: Barcelona's main annual festival around 24 September, encompassing many events such as human towers (castellers), free live music events on the streets, firework displays, and processions of wooden giants. It is a holiday and the

candidates.name: Festes de Gràcia
candidates.content: The Festes de Gracia is a Catalonian celebration, held around 15 August each year to commemorate the Assumption. During the week of festivities that mark one of Barcelona's most important fiestas, the city of Gracia explodes with

candidates.name: Fira de Santa Llúcia
candidates.content: From 2/3 December to 23 December, to commemorate St. Llúcia (13 December). During this time, in front of the Cathedral, Christmas objects are sold. Some places sell Christmas trees, but most of them sell elements for making the pe

candidates.name: Parc del Laberint d'Horta
candidates.content: Try out the labyrinth in the centre of this park. The park also has a nice waterfall, a romantic canal and gardens. A quiet place to relax for several hours away from the busy city. Wheelchair accessible. Free of charge on Wednesd

candidates.name: Festes de Sants
candidates.content: Similar to Gracia's event, but smaller and later on in August. If you can't go to Gracia's event, try to go to this festival.

candidates.name: Fira de Barcelona
candidates.content: There are trade events all year round in Barcelona.

candidates.name: La Rambla
candidates.content: A gorgeous tree-lined pedestrian walkway, the busiest and most lively street of the city. Mostly occupied by tourists, expect to pay higher prices for food and drink which tends to be low-quality and/or inauthentic. Avoid the grou

candidates.name: Walk around el Born
candidates.content: A very popular area with great restaurants and places to have a few drinks. If your accommodation is on Rambla, Born is a great place to escape the crowds, enjoy a relaxed atmosphere and meet off-the-beaten track travellers and no

candidates.name: Tibidabo
candidates.content: Located on the mountains of Barcelona (farther north from Gracia) and offers a spectacular view of the city (532 m high). This is a place where according to some legends, the Devil tempted Jesus Christ offering him the whole world

candidates.name: Spanish Civil War tours
candidates.content: Walking tour of Barcelona visiting key sites relating to the Spanish Civil War, covering themes such as Anarchism, the International Brigades, George Orwell and the realities of daily life and bombing during the war.

candidates.name: Barcelona Jazz Festival
candidates.price: Tickets prices differ for each event
candidates.content: A brighter way to celebrate the colder Autumn days, the annual Jazz festival has been running for nearly 50 years now and runs roughly from the last week in October and all the way through November

candidates.name: El Portal de l'Àngel
candidates.content: Large pedestrian walkway with many new and stylish shops to browse in.

candidates.name: Enjoy your Sangria at La Plaça Reial
candidates.content: Great place to sit, relax and drink.

candidates.name: CosmoCaixa
candidates.price: €8 for general admission. Some exhibitions & activities have an additional charge.
candidates.content: Isaac Newton 26; Perhaps one of the best science museums in Europe. Order tickets online to avoid the queue. Depending on your level of interest, you can spend there up to half a day. Plenty of fun interactive elements. Weekends m

candidates.name: Artoba Tours
candidates.content: City and day tours of Barcelona and Catalonia led by a professional archaeologist.

candidates.name: Sant Jordi
candidates.content: 23 April. Considered to be like Valentine's Day. People give roses and books around the streets. Traditionally, men give women roses and women give men books. It is one of the most popular and interesting celebrations in Catalonia

candidates.name: Corpus
candidates.content: Late in May (Corpus Christi day). An egg shell is placed over the jet of water coming out of various fountains such that the egg "magically dances" over the water. These fountains typically are beautifully decorated with flowers a

candidates.name: L'Antic Teatre
candidates.content: Screens special artistic productions. There is also a small café inside and outside operated by the association which makes for a great break from the noisy Barcelona downtown. It's only a few steps away from the Palau de la Músic

candidates.name: Catwalk
candidates.content: One of the most popular nightclubs in the city, with the peak time around 02:00. They offer 2 floors with R&B and hip-hop styles mixed with House or Techno. A lot of teenagers go here.

candidates.name: La Fianna
candidates.content: One of the busiest bars in the neighborhood with a funky decor and a large selection of spirits. They also have a great dinner menu with an international selection.

candidates.name: RiBborn
candidates.content: C/Antic de Sant Joan 3. A hip bar in the heart of the Casc Antic, a vibrant section of the Ciutat Vella with a variety of bars and restaurants. RiBborn offers "Funk you till you drop" hiphop jazz reggae and soul with dj Chocolito

candidates.name: Club Sauvage
candidates.content: One of the best choices for drinks and music in Casc Antic. Offers live music (4 or 5 nights a week, 22:00-00:30). Hosts DJ sessions every night (daily 00:30-04:30/05:00) with DJs of many different styles and from the most importa

candidates.name: Travel Bar
candidates.content: Travel Bar is a good place to meet and talk with other people visiting the city. They offer free walking tours guided by long-term 'ex-pat' residents of the city every day at 11:00, 13:00 and 15:00. Has a nice, open terrace. Very

candidates.name: Irish Pub Temple Bar
candidates.content: An Irish pub near Las Ramblas. A space where you can enjoy the best national and international beers, smash burgers, while you watch live games from our big screens.

candidates.name: El Dorado
candidates.content: With an ample dance floor, it also has a pool table, 'futbolín' and arcade games. The giant video screens and the monitors over the bar are other icons of this music bar. Drinks are catered for by staff that are professional, like

candidates.name: Café del Sol
candidates.content: An emblem, Cafè del Sol was one of the first bars to open in this famous and very popular Gràcia squares. There is a decent choice of tapas or sandwiches too. Inside has a marble bar, outside many chairs on the placa.

candidates.name: Razzmatazz
candidates.content: Large and popular club with several rooms, each one a different style of music (pop, retro, house, trance). It is loved by the visitors and locals. €15 will get you in with a free drink. It's worth paying an entry fee. Saturdays a

candidates.name: Maumau
candidates.content: A chilled out lounge bar with groovy tunes that uses its space to host short film nights, installations and concerts. Their webpage is worth a look for upcoming events and shows in Barcelona.

candidates.name: Comerç 24
candidates.content: A fashion tapas bar. Very creative, very good.

candidates.name: Danzantoria
candidates.content: House music fans come here for the pumping beats and funky decor. Offers two floors of dancing, and a terrace to chill out on between dances.

candidates.name: Le Kashbar
candidates.content: With a Moroccan decor, Le Kashbar is the perfect spot to chill out on cushions and take in the ambient music.

candidates.name: The Clubhouse Laietana & Nikki's
candidates.content: The Clubhouse has teamed up with Nikki's and now supply a variety of budget friendly North American soul food. Here you can get fried chicken burgers, fried chicken & waffles, mac & cheese and a whole bunch of other delicious opti

candidates.name: Els Quatre Gats
candidates.content: Frequented by tourists, Els Quatre Gats, is the successor to the famous cafe where Gaudi drank and Picasso exhibited, in a fine Modernisme building by Puig i Cadafalch. The cooking is of a high quality (if it's not onion soup). Th

candidates.name: La Taberna del Cura
candidates.price: 1st courses €4-12; main courses €12-20; salad, filet, small bottle wine, water, dessert, coffee - €50
candidates.content: Known by locals as one of the better restaurants in town, the menu is mostly meat selections, but seafood can be ordered from its sister restaurant Botafumeiro next door. La Taberna is on the expensive side, but the food is excell

candidates.name: Somodo
candidates.price: lunch menu €18.50, tasting dinner menu €25 (excluding taxes)
candidates.content: The small hidden gem has 19 tables, hence reservation is highly recommended. The chef Hojiro Ochi serves Mediterranean cuisine with Japanese influences. The tasting menu consists of 3 entrées, 2 main dishes (fish and meat) and 3 d

candidates.name: Flash-Flash
candidates.content: Not really in Gràcia, but next to it, it's one of the restaurants of the Tuset street years, when the Gauche Divine was the cool group in the city. This restaurant was made as a cool bar during the late 1960s and it remains unchan

candidates.name: La Porteria
candidates.content: This quiet street holds a few bars and restaurants to choose from. La Porteria is nothing fancy, but seems to keep a steady local crowd. They have a menu del noche (like the menu del dia), which provides a good value and the propr

candidates.name: Mirablau
candidates.content: Food and service are average but the stunning views make up for it with floor-to-ceiling windows providing a sweeping view of Barcelona. Popular spot with locals for a drink and some romantic ambiance.

candidates.name: Taberna Blai Tonight
candidates.content: A big variety of tapas including cheese, tortillas, seafood and meat options are offered by friendly staff. First one has to choose a plate and a drink. At the end one pays for the number of toothpicks. Cheap drinks attracts a you

candidates.name: Barcelona Eat Local Food Tours
candidates.content: A family-owned business that showcases the best of Catalan gastronomy in off-the-beaten districts of Barcelona.

candidates.name: Mercado de La Boqueria
candidates.content: On the Rambla, and offering a wide variety of fresh, mainly raw foods. Some stall sells many kinds of well cooked ready to eat pasta, fresh fruit already sliced. When buying anything here head to the cheaper stalls at the back: yo

candidates.name: Restaurante La Boqueria
candidates.content: An emblematic restaurant in the centre of Barcelona to enjoy the city's local cuisine. Approximately €20 per person to eat dishes like Paella or Tapas.

candidates.name: Can Culleretes
candidates.content: Founded in 1786, it is the second oldest restaurant in Spain (after Casa Botín in Madrid). The prices are mid range and the quality is quite good for the price. They serve traditional Catalan food. But the most interesting from th

candidates.name: La Boqueria
candidates.content: In Ciutat Vella. Large public market with a diverse range of goods and produce. Enjoy freshly squeezed organic fruit juices for €1.5 per cup. If you go near closing time (20:00) sellers will make you a special price (2 or 3 for €2

candidates.name: Maremagnum
candidates.content: Nice shopping mall by the sea at the end of The Ramblas. The only shopping mall in the city open on Sunday and public holidays. Clothes: mostly mass-market brands; no independent designers; only a few outlets of national chains

candidates.name: La Boqueria Market
candidates.content: Tempt your tastebuds at this delightful food market where the food is plentiful, fresh and can be cooked to order in one of about five small restaurants. Also a place for fresh juices and some takeaway snacks. To avoid heavy crowd

candidates.name: La Concepcio
candidates.content: The local market in the heart of the Eixample sells fresh fruits, vegetables and seafood. This is a great flower market too, the florists are open all week. The market is over than 120 years old, but has been thoroughly modernized

candidates.name: GreenLifeStyle
candidates.content: The shops philosophy is based on principles of sustainability, recycling and fair trade, which all sold items adhere. One finds cute designer dresses for a fair price.
